trial_court: District Judge, Kokrajhar, Assam (Title Suit No. 22/2017)
case_name: Smti. Uma Ray vs Mridul Ray
facts_of_case: Matrimonial dispute between husband and wife; divorce granted by trial court with permanent alimony of Rs.5,00,000/-; appeal filed for enhancement of alimony.

legal_principles.principle: Enhancement of maintenance under Section 25(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is a substantive right which cannot be denied.
legal_principles.held: A similar view was expressed by the Himachal Pradesh High Court in the Case of Kubza Devi vs Isher Dass reported in AIR 2017 (HP) 21, wherein it has been held that the maintenance fixed by the order of the court can be enhanced in changed circumstances under Section 25 (2) of the Act, 1955 and that the principle of estoppels would not be attracted.
cited_cases: P. Achala alias Atchamamba vs Varada Siva Rama Krishna , (2008) AIR 216 (AP)
Kubza Devi vs Isher Dass, (2017) AIR 21 (HP)

legal_principles.principle: The wife's right to future maintenance is a matter of public concern which she cannot barter away.
legal_principles.held: It was observed- 'The wife's right to future maintenance is a matter of public concern which she cannot barter away'.
cited_cases: P. Achala alias Atchamamba vs Varada Siva Rama Krishna , (2008) AIR 216 (AP)
Kubza Devi vs Isher Dass, (2017) AIR 21 (HP)

legal_principles.principle: The principle of estoppels would not be attracted in the case of enhancement of maintenance.
legal_principles.held: It has been held that the principle of estoppels would not be attracted.
cited_cases: Kubza Devi vs Isher Dass, (2017) AIR 21 (HP)

legal_principles.principle: The court has to ascertain the financial capacity/status of both parties for fixing maintenance.
legal_principles.held: In matrimonial cases, the court has to ascertain the financial capacity/status of both the parties for fixing maintenance.

outcome.final_order: Permanent alimony amount to be enhanced (amount not specified); no other relief claimed or granted.
